summary: Reallocates the Miles sound-system sample array: tears down the existing 20-byte-entry array at this+0x48 (releasing per-entry virtual sub-objects and AIL sample handles, then freeing the array header), stores the new count into this+0x4C, allocates a fresh zero-filled array via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper, and, for each new entry, allocates and initializes an AIL sample handle when the driver handle at this+0x90 is set.

operations.description: Guard: only tear down the existing sample array when this[0x48] (array pointer) is non-null.
Loop while the entry count this[0x4C] > 0 (guard), stepping 20 bytes per entry, to tear down each entry of the existing array.
For each entry holding a live sub-object (vtable pointer non-null), invoke its virtual release routine via vtable slot +8 (indirect call, no named packet callee).
Call AIL_release_sample_handle (global 0x0059E3F0) on each entry's sample handle at entry+16 and clear that handle slot.
Free the array header memory by calling FreeWrapper_7bcf (callee 0x00587BCF) on this[0x48]-4.
Null this[0x48] after teardown, then store the new count a2 into this[0x4C].
If a2 > 0, allocate 20*a2+4 bytes via OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper (callee 0x00587C03), storing a2 in the allocation header and zero-filling every 20-byte entry.
Store the new array pointer into this[0x48], or 0 when allocation fails.
When the allocation succeeded and the driver handle this[0x90] is set, allocate an AIL sample handle via AIL_allocate_sample_handle (global 0x0059E3EC) into each entry+16.
Initialize each newly allocated sample handle via AIL_init_sample (global 0x0059E3DC).

clean_pseudocode: if (this[0x48]) for each entry: if (this[0x90]) { entry+16 = AIL_allocate_sample_handle(this[0x90]); AIL_init_sample(entry+16); }
